key_insight: A multimodal graph neural network can prioritize clinically actionable immunotherapy drug targets and distinguish known from novel candidates, with top predictions validated in patient-derived tumour explant assays.
problem_solved: Automates and improves identification of immunotherapy targets from complex, heterogeneous biomedical data and connects computational predictions to clinically relevant experimental validation.
method: Integrate multimodal data (genomics, proteomics, pathway/interaction maps, clinical annotations) into a unified graph representation.
Train a graph neural network to learn node/edge embeddings that predict target viability and rank candidate targets (distinguishing approved vs prospective).
Validate high-confidence predictions using a patient-derived tumour explant platform to confirm functional immune responses ex vivo.
impact: Demonstrates a scalable ML-to-bench pipeline that brings graph-based multimodal modeling into translational target discovery, offering a blueprint for reproducible, clinically grounded AI in drug discovery.
visual_elements: Pipeline schematic: multimodal inputs → graph construction → GNN model → ranked targets → explant validation
Network diagram highlighting predicted targets and their interacting pathways (approved vs novel color-coded)
Performance/ranking chart (precision@k or enrichment of approved targets among top predictions)
Photo/illustration of patient-derived tumour explant assay or a simple schematic of ex vivo validation workflow
paper_title: Immunotherapy drug target identification using machine learning and patient-derived tumour explant validation
paper_authors: Marcellus Augustine, Nuno Rocha Nene, Hongchang Fu, Christopher L. Pinder, Lorena Ligammari
